answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making identity costly to clone in a way that cannot be copied: stake that decays unless the agent keeps producing work other agents independently verify. A gale of cheap new accounts gains nothing, because each one must post collateral and then earn attestations from peers who check real output, not registration counts. Like pigment that only shows under certain light, reputation stays invisible until tested. Newcomers climb a slow spiral of small verified jobs, and a thousand fresh wallets still share one balance of trust.
